## Independent research

**Does the Crowd Add to the Forecast? Probability Forecasts in Kalshi Weather Markets**
[In progress]{.status .status-progress} 2026–present\
*M.S. capstone and writing sample* ·
[working paper (PDF)](files/Ramirez_Kalshi_Weather_Forecasts_v7.pdf)

- Designed the research questions, forecast comparisons, test specifications and
  scoring rules for a study of Kalshi daily-high-temperature contracts against public
  NOAA forecasts.
- Constructed a matched dataset of market quotes, public forecast vintages and
  settlement outcomes for 1,435 event-days across four cities.
- On 139 chronologically held-out New York event-days, Kalshi's mean multicategory
  Brier score was 14.5% below the National Blend of Models' (time-block bootstrap,
  HAC inference).
- Built a calibrated six-source public benchmark; Kalshi outperforms it in New York
  and Los Angeles, with inconclusive differences in Miami and Phoenix.

**Replication of Luco and Marshall (2020), "The Competitive Impact of Vertical
Integration by Multiproduct Firms"** [In progress]{.status .status-progress} 2026–present

- Reproduced selected reduced-form specifications in R using `fixest`, including
  Tables 4A, 4B and 6, with product-store, product-week and store-week fixed effects
  and county-clustered inference.
- Examined treatment definitions, comparison-group restrictions, pretrend diagnostics
  and indirect treatment through rival-price responses; maintained a
  published-versus-reproduced comparison record.

More detail, including what isn't finished, is on [Research & Projects](research.qmd).
